bib.title: PaperBench: Evaluating AI's Ability to Replicate AI Research

read.skipped: Per-paper result tables 10-18 skimmed for structure only; references skimmed for lineage.

question: Can AI agents replicate state-of-the-art ML research papers from scratch, and how do we grade that at scale?
contributions: PaperBench: 20 ML papers with author-approved rubrics and an automated LLM-judge grading workflow
PaperBench Code-Dev: lighter variant grading only code development
JudgeEval: human-graded dataset to assess automated judges
Evaluations of frontier models on PaperBench

method.summary: Agents get a paper plus addendum and must write a repository with reproduce.sh. The submission is re-run in a fresh VM (A10 GPU) and an LLM judge grades each leaf of a weighted rubric tree as pass/fail; scores propagate as weighted averages to a root Replication Score.
method.task: from-scratch replication of ML papers by agents (long-horizon ML R&D), rubric-graded

datasets.name: PaperBench
datasets.split: all 20 (ICML 2024 Spotlight/Oral); plus 2 NeurIPS 2024 Workshop papers as dev set; held-out set kept internally
datasets.source: ICML 2024; 20 of 42 contacted authors co-developed rubrics
datasets.preprocessing: Filtered by commercial/geographic, empirical content, single-machine hardware, no closed-source model dependency, no human data, reproducibility, non-framework, accessible dependencies (gpt-4o-2024-08-06 prompts then manual read)

datasets.name: JudgeEval
datasets.size: partial replications of 4 PaperBench papers + 1 dev paper (number of leaf nodes not stated)
datasets.split: human-graded leaf nodes as ground truth
datasets.source: replications written from scratch or by modifying authors' codebases

other.response_parser: gpt-4o-2024-08-06 extracts score, explanation, valid-score flag

inference.samples: 3 runs per paper per model (2 seeds for o1 IterativeAgent and Gemini BasicAgent per Table 9); average Replication Score across papers; SEM reported
inference.prompting: BasicAgent: ReAct tool loop based on Inspect AI basic agent, with end_task tool, context trimming, paginated file reader; tools: bash, Python, web browser, file reader. IterativeAgent: no end-task tool, 'take next step' prompt. Task instructions in Figs 13-14.

parameters.api_credit_given: HuggingFace key and OpenAI API with $1000
parameters.reproduce_runtime_cap: 12 hours in experiments (task text says 7 days)
parameters.judge_file_filter: whitelist source files; if too big for context minus 10,000 tokens, judge ranks files and top ten are used
parameters.blacklist_monitor: text search of agent logs for blacklisted URLs, manual review, disqualified scored 0

other.human_baseline: 8 ML PhD participants, 4 papers, 3 attempts per paper, part-time over 4-week window, best@3; A10 GPU (A100 for four attempts); AI assistants allowed; snapshots graded at various hours

metrics.name: Replication Score
metrics.definition: Weighted average of leaf pass/fail scores propagated up the rubric tree; averaged across papers

metrics.name: F1 / accuracy / precision / recall (JudgeEval)
metrics.definition: Binary classification of leaf nodes against human labels, macro-averaged over papers

baselines: Human ML PhDs (best@3, 48 h) on subset
eval.protocol: Reproduce.sh executed in fresh VM, LLM judge grades each leaf; 3 runs per paper; SEM; Code-Dev variant skips reproduction and grades only Code Development nodes.

availability.code: open-sourced (Abstract: 'We open-source our code'); URL not given in the text
availability.data: open-sourced with code; URL not given in text

prompts.text: SYSTEM: You are judging an attempt to reproduce a research paper. ... respond with a list of filepaths separated by newlines in descending order of importance.
prompts.where: Figure 7 (abridged here; full text in paper)

prompts.text: Be strict and thorough in grading your resolution criteria, but do not check for things that are outside of your scope.
You are a helpful agent attempting to solve a task. ... Use as much of the available time as possible to refine and optimize your solution ... ACTUALLY REPLICATE the paper YOURSELF
Now given the previous progress made by the agent, take the next step towards replicating the paper
You are tasked with reproducing a research paper. ... Your task is to replicate as many of the core contributions of this paper as possible

limits: Only 20 papers; authors argue thousands of rubric requirements mitigate this.
Contamination: authors' codebases exist online; future models may have internalised them.
Rubric creation takes an expert several full days each; hard to train others; hard to replicate the process.
LLM judge less accurate than an expert human (F1 0.83), non-deterministic; Code Development is the weakest type (F1 0.72).
Cost: about $8000 per eval run for o1 IterativeAgent plus about $66 per paper grading.
Human baseline is small (8 participants, 3 papers for the headline comparison), part-time, assigned to papers they felt confident about.
Claude 3.7 Sonnet could not be evaluated due to API rate limits; agent scaffolds only lightly tuned, so scores are initial baselines not capability ceilings.
Rubric child order encodes dependencies only implicitly; specification-gaming loopholes cannot be ruled out.
High variance across runs on same paper; Code-Dev only weakly correlated with full score.
